title: China’s new AI bottleneck isn’t chips. It’s running out of Chinese-language training data.
excerpt: Chinese accounts for just 1.3% of global web content. Beijing is now treating data as strategic infrastructure, with a 2028 plan to build national AI datasets.
content_html:
TL;DR

China faces a critical AI data shortage. Chinese is just 1.3% of web content vs 49% English. Beijing plans national datasets by 2028. WeChat and Douyin don’t share data externally. Publishers are adding AI training bans.

China’s AI race has a new constraint, and it is not chips. The country is running out of high-quality Chinese-language training data. While US export controls on advanced semiconductors have dominated the debate over China’s AI capabilities, Chinese experts are increasingly warning that data scarcity could prove equally limiting, and unlike chips, there is no hardware workaround. Chinese accounts for just 1.3% of global web content, according to internet tracker W3Techs, compared to nearly half for English, 6% for Spanish, and 5% for Japanese.

The problem is global but hits China harder. Epoch AI estimates the worldwide supply of high-quality, publicly available text could be fully exhausted within six years. OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy has warned of a “data wall” by decade’s end. Chinese developers already pay more per useful token than Western counterparts because their models must work harder with less native-language material. China’s digital ecosystem makes the shortage worse: platforms like WeChat and Douyin do not share data with third-party developers, leaving AI labs to train on lower-quality sources.

Beijing is responding by treating data as strategic infrastructure. In June, the National Data Administration unveiled a nationwide plan to build validated AI training datasets by 2028, covering manufacturing, energy, healthcare, finance, agriculture, autonomous driving, and embodied AI. “Competition in the AI era is not only about models and computing power, but also about high-quality data supply systems,” said Yu Xiaohui, president of the state-affiliated China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. Tsinghua University computer scientist Sun Maosong has urged authorities to digitise historical archives, ancient manuscripts, scientific literature, and regional dialects.

Not everyone wants to be digitised. Huaxia Publishing House recently added a warning to a new translation: “It is prohibited to use the content of this book for artificial intelligence training. Violators will be held legally responsible.” China is already anxious about American AI models it cannot match, and the data shortage explains part of the gap. The US has Anthropic’s Project Panama, which bought and destroyed millions of physical books to scan them. China has 1.3% of the web and a publishing industry that is starting to lock the door.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

中国面临人工智能数据严重短缺的问题。 中文仅占网页内容的 1.3%，而英文则占 49%。 北京计划到 2028 年建立国家数据集。 微信和抖音不对外共享数据。 出版商正在增加人工智能培训禁令。

中国的AI竞赛有了新的制约因素，而且不是芯片。 该国的高质量中文培训数据即将耗尽。 尽管美国对先进半导体的出口管制主导了有关中国人工智能能力的争论，但中国专家越来越多地警告说，数据稀缺可能同样具有限制性，而且与芯片不同的是，没有硬件解决办法。 根据互联网跟踪机构 W3Techs 的数据，中文仅占全球网络内容的 1.3%，而英语占全球网络内容的近一半，西班牙语占 6%，日语占 5%。

这个问题是全球性的，但对中国的影响更大。 Epoch AI 估计，全球高质量、公开可用的文本供应可能会在六年内完全耗尽。 OpenAI 联合创始人安德烈·卡帕蒂 (Andrej Karpathy) 警告称，到本世纪末，“数据墙”将会出现。 中国开发者已经为每个有用的代币支付了比西方同行更高的费用，因为他们的模型必须在使用更少的母语材料的情况下更加努力。 中国的数字生态系统使这种短缺变得更加严重：微信和抖音等平台不与第三方开发者共享数据，导致人工智能实验室只能在质量较低的来源上进行培训。

北京的回应是将数据视为战略基础设施。 6月，国家数据管理局公布了一项全国计划，到2028年建立经过验证的人工智能训练数据集，涵盖制造、能源、医疗、金融、农业、自动驾驶和实体人工智能。 “人工智能时代的竞争不仅是模型和算力的竞争，更是高质量数据供给系统的竞争。”中国信息通信研究院院长余晓辉表示。 清华大学计算机科学家孙茂松敦促当局将历史档案、古代手稿、科学文献和地方方言数字化。

并不是每个人都希望被数字化。 华夏出版社近日在新译本中添加了警告：“禁止将本书内容用于人工智能训练。 违者将追究法律责任。” 中国已经对无法匹敌的美国人工智能模型感到焦虑，而数据短缺解释了部分差距。 美国有 Anthropic 的巴拿马计划，该计划购买并销毁了数百万本实体书以进行扫描。 中国拥有 1.3% 的网络份额，而出版业也开始紧闭大门。
